title: purchase-lane-fallback-matrix
summary: Working matrix for purchase lanes and fallback sequencing across regions. Purpose: codify how we will route orders when primary vendor lanes degrade (longer lead-times, allocation shortfalls) and explicitly list trigger thresholds, expected lead-time distributions, and cost uplift for each fallback. This sheet is intentionally operational — contains conservative assumptions for SLO planning and quick lookup for on-call and procurement.
purpose_and_scope: Scope: GPU fleet purchases (discrete orders and reserved commitments) across NA-east, NA-west, EU, APAC. Excludes short-term cloud instance bursts and internal fleet reshuffles (separate playbook). Use to decide: 1) when to convert committed lanes to expedite, 2) which secondary vendors to engage, 3) finance commit windows for early orders.
purchase_lanes_overview: Lane A - Vendor Direct (monthly commitments): typical lead-time 8-12 weeks, min order 40 units, price baseline. Lane B - Channel Partners (regional distributors): lead-time 4-10 weeks variable, smaller MOQ (8-32), slightly higher unit price, flexible shipping. Lane C - Broker/Refurb mix: lead-time 2-6 weeks, heterogeneous SKU quality, +15-30% cost, higher reject rate. Lane D - Short-term Lease/Cloud credits: immediate availability but much higher effective cost per token; used only for urgent SLO protection. Lane E - Manufacturing Holdback (negotiated retention slots): multi-quarter horizon, used for strategic SKU continuity.
lead_time_assumptions: Assumptions used in modelling: Vendor Direct LTA follows approx normal-ish distribution with median 10 weeks, sigma 2.5w. Channel partners show right-skew (median 6w, heavy tail to 12w). Brokers are bimodal (immediate small lots or 4-6w). Leasing is effectively zero lead-time but billed monthly. We assume transit customs adds 1-3 weeks for EU/APAC inbound unless pre-cleared.
reorder_triggers_and_thresholds: Trigger rules (examples): - Reorder when available-runway <= 12 weeks given current burn rate and committed orders in-transit. - If Vendor Direct ETA slips > 25% beyond expected, automatically open Channel Partner lane at 2x priority and notify finance to consider partial prepay. - If combined committed + in-transit < projected demand for a coming quarter (P50), escalate to Head of Infrastructure with proposed broker fill plan. - For APAC, apply stricter buffer: reorder at 16-week runway due to longer customs variability.
fallback_priority_matrix: Priority order: 1) Channel Partners (Lane B) for same-SKU shortfalls, 2) Broker/Refurb (Lane C) when SKU mix can tolerate substitutions, 3) Short-term Lease (Lane D) to protect critical latency-sensitive routes, 4) Manufacturing Holdback (Lane E) only for strategic long-term SKU preservation. Each fallback entry includes expected cost uplift: B +10-18%, C +20-35% (depending on refurb rate), D effective +200-400% borne to application cost center.
regional_special_considerations: NA-east: strong vendor coverage, low customs friction. NA-west: prioritized for Hosted API burst zones; prefer shorter transit. EU: allow wider reorder buffer (14-16w), prioritize distributors with EU warehousing. APAC: plan for port congestion windows (monsoon, holidays); prefer brokers with local stock for <6w fills.
example_order_pipeline_snapshot: (hand-entered snapshot) - 2025-02-01: Vendor Direct order #VD-431 (80 units) ETA 2025-04-10; Channel Partner options open: CP-Delta (20 units available in 3w), CP-Atlas (40 units 6-8w). - Current burn projection (prod load): 900 units/quarter global. Safety target: 1.2x quarter burn in committed+reserved. - Current gap estimated: 260 units for Q2 if all ETAs hold.
risk_scoring_and_mitigation: Risk scoring heuristics: Impact * Likelihood -> Tier. Impact high if shortfall affects dedicated customer SLAs or >15% of global capacity. Likelihood factors: vendor allocation signals, historical lead-time variance, macro factors (chip shortage cycle). Mitigations: staggered delivery cadence, prioritized SKU mapping (reduce specialized SKU exposure by 30% where possible), contractual reserved slots with penalty clauses.
cost_accounting_notes: When selecting fallback lanes, capture cost uplift to the consuming product route. Finance needs line item: 'procurement uplift' bucket applied to relevant customer cohorts. For leases, amortize effective per-token cost across expected leased run window and tag to the temporary capacity cost center.

notes_to_oncall_and_procurement: Quick lookup guidance: if SLA risk alert triggers (model latency degradation > 20% sustained), immediately open Lane B quoting and inform SRE-runbook. Do not deploy Lane D (leasing) without Director approval unless outage risk is classified critical. Keep this sheet as the canonical fallback sequence and snapshot your decisions into the procurement ticket.
freeform_observations: Observed that channel lead-times improved slightly in winter shipping window; however, manufacturers indicated backlog shift into late Q2. Consider smoothing burn via temporary batching rules on low-priority embed jobs.
versioning_and_audit_instructions: When you edit, append a timestamped line to decisions_log and update last_modified. Keep copies of vendor quotes attached to the procurement JIRA tickets. For audits, export this sheet CSV for the quarter alongside finance approvals.
